doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Grimes at Mastbaum and Juilliard
summary: Grimes describes his pre-college vocational school, then Juilliard choral and opera orchestra playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Henry, you spent some time in a couple of music schools, right? Mastbaum? Is that how you say it?
Yeah Mastbaum, that was my pre-college school, then I went to Juilliard.
Mastbaum was like a vocational school, right?
Well when you went to Juilliard, were you learning what you wanted to learn?

When I went to Juilliard I did, yes, I did. I was doing things, for instance I was, well I played the bass for choral groups and one day rehearsed, we did this chorus, I’d be the only bass player playing with these chorus groups. And that was a very challenging kind of a thing to do, you know? And but also when I went to Juilliard also I played in an opera orchestra. And it was only about two or three basses in that. And I played with that, reading, you know a lot of reading music. Music school is that way you know, which I enjoyed very much. Because it was the first thing I ever touched in a real technical sense. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
You know I never had that kind of feeling before, just playing something and the feeling that it just doesn’t go over that way, or some other way.
It must have been good for your bowing chops too.
Oh yeah, it was good for everything.
